tokyo-kanto-rides-tomiura-to-nojimazaki-.story: Scenery first, traffic last, with checkpoints that make sense on a bike. Out of Kimitsu and back again: 591 km, roughly 10 h 45 in the saddle. It goes by way of Ōhara, Scenic stretch near Ishige and Annaka. near Ami is the high point. It tops out at about 1,250 m. Long stretches are under trees.

tokyo-kanto-rides-tomiura-to-nojimazaki-.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: Treat High point near Ami → Scenic stretch near Ishige as bend craft. Brake early, look high through the turn, and keep throttle changes gentle. It is more satisfying to link ten clean bends than rescue one silly one.

sections.to: Near Annaka, on the way back
sections.advice: Scenic stretch near Ishige → Near Annaka, on the way back is the reward section in Tokyo. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

sections.from: Near Annaka, on the way back

sections.advice: Photo stop near Enzan → Near Kawaguchi is shade riding: beautiful, cooler and sometimes slick. Expect damp patches, leaves, gravel and wildlife where the trees meet the road.

safetyMarkers.note: Respect posted limits and assume enforcement near villages, viewpoints and main-road joins.

scenicChapters.title: Teterow market fuel → back through Güstrow old town meal stop
scenicChapters.narrative: 75 km through ground somebody thought worth listing. The road passes it rather than bypassing it — speed drops and stays down. Park rather than crawl through.

scenicChapters.title: back through Güstrow old town meal stop → back through Sternberg lake
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 70 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
